title: Understanding and Tackling Over-Dilution in Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Message Passing Neural Networks struggle with unintended behaviors caused by irregular graph data structures, including over-smoothing and over-squashing.

gap.claim: Limitations of MPNNs involving the dilution of information specific to an individual node within a single layer have previously been overlooked.

contributions.claim: The paper presents and formulates the concept of over-dilution using intra-node dilution for attribute-level representations and inter-node dilution for node-level representations.
The paper introduces a transformer-based solution intended to alleviate over-dilution and complement existing node embedding methods such as MPNNs.
The paper provides new insights into limitations of MPNNs and informative graph representations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report observing significant dilution of information specific to an individual node within a single layer.
The authors report that their findings provide new insights and contribute to the development of informative representations.
The implementation and supplementary materials are publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: MPNNs are important for graph machine learning but exhibit unintended behaviors such as over-smoothing and over-squashing.
The paper investigates previously overlooked limitations of MPNNs.
Information specific to an individual node can become significantly diluted within a single layer.
The paper names and formulates this phenomenon as over-dilution with intra-node and inter-node dilution factors.
A transformer-based solution is introduced to alleviate over-dilution and complement existing node embedding methods.
